items.title: 14.2.1 Dot or Scalar Product of Two Vectors and Its Geometrical Interpretation (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Ab hum vector multiplication ki pehli qisam shuru karte hain. Kitab batati hai ke do vectors ke yeh products asal mein physics aur engineering ki zaroorat se paida hue, aur do vectors ke darmiyan angle ka tasawwur (idea) bhi isi scalar product ke zariye likha jata hai. Is sabaq ke baad aap do vectors ka dot product do tareeqon se nikal sakenge aur samjhenge ke dono tareeqe ek hi jawab kyun dete hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh idea aaya kahan se? Physics mein jab ek force \(\underline{F}\) kisi cheez ko \(\underline{d}\) faasle tak le jati hai to us ka work (kaam) \(|\underline{F}||\underline{d}|\cos\theta\) hota hai, jahan \(\theta\) force aur harkat (motion) ke darmiyan angle hai. Wajah yeh hai ke force ka sirf woh hissa kaam karta hai jo harkat ki seedh mein ho. Mathematics ne do vectors ke is combination ko ek naam de diya: dot product. Is ka jawab ek number hota hai, isi liye isay scalar product bhi kehte hain.

Farz karein do non-zero vectors \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) (plane mein hon ya space mein) ka initial point (shuru ka point) ek hi hai, yani dono ek hi jagah se nikalte hain. To \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ka dot product, jise \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) likhte hain (parhein "u dot v"), yun define hota hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "have some initial point" chhapa hai. Sahi lafz "same" hai: dono vectors ka initial point ek hi (same) hona chahiye, kyun ke angle tabhi sahi naapa jata hai jab dono vectors ek hi point se shuru hon.

blocks.text_alt: u dot v equals the magnitude of u times the magnitude of v times cos theta

blocks.alt: Three drawings of vectors u and v drawn from the same point. In the first the angle theta between them is acute, in the second it is obtuse, and in the third u and v point in opposite directions so theta equals pi. A curved arrow marks theta in each.
blocks.caption: Figure: the angle θ between u and v, measured with both vectors starting at the same point (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Yahan \(\theta\) vectors \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ke darmiyan angle hai aur \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\), yani angle \(0^{\circ}\) se \(180^{\circ}\) tak hota hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "Where θ in the angle" chhapa hai; sahi jumla "where θ is the angle" hai (θ angle hai).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is definition ko teen baaton se samjhiye:
1. Dono vectors ko tail to tail rakhein (dono ki dum ek hi point par). Agar figure mein ek vector doosre ke sire se shuru ho raha ho (head to tail), to pehle use khiska kar (slide kar ke) dono ki dum mila lein. Warna aap \(\theta\) ki jagah \(\pi - \theta\) naap lenge, aur cos ka sign ulat jayega.
2. \(\theta\) hamesha \(0\) aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan liya jata hai. Is se bara angle lene ki zaroorat nahin, kyun ke do vectors ke darmiyan chhota wala angle hi "the angle" kehlata hai.
3. \(|\underline{u}|\) aur \(|\underline{v}|\) lambaiyan hain, hamesha positive. Is liye \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) ka sign wahi hai jo \(\cos\theta\) ka sign hai. Upar ki teeno figures teeno soorton ko dikhati hain: chhota angle, bara angle, aur bilkul ulti simt (\(\theta = \pi\)).

blocks.caption: Hamara khulasa: dot product ka sign angle se tay hota hai

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) bilkul ek hi simt mein hon (\(\theta = 0\)), to \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) kya hoga? Aur agar bilkul ulti simt mein hon (\(\theta = \pi\))? Jawab: \(\cos 0 = 1\), is liye \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\), sab se bari value. Aur \(\cos\pi = -1\), is liye \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = -|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\), sab se chhoti value. Baqi har angle ke liye jawab in dono ke darmiyan hota hai.

Ab wahi product components (hisson) se. (a) Agar plane mein do non-zero vectors \(\underline{u} = a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{v} = a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j}\) hon, to dot product \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) yun define hota hai:

blocks.text_alt: u dot v equals a 1 a 2 plus b 1 b 2

blocks.text: (b) Agar space mein do non-zero vectors \(\underline{u} = a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k}\) aur \(\underline{v} = a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j} + c_{2}\underline{k}\) hon, to dot product \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) yun define hota hai:

blocks.text_alt: u dot v equals a 1 a 2 plus b 1 b 2 plus c 1 c 2

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Dot product ko scalar product ya inner product bhi kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Definition 2 asal kaam ka formula hai: \(\underline{i}\) wale component ko \(\underline{i}\) wale se, \(\underline{j}\) wale ko \(\underline{j}\) wale se, \(\underline{k}\) wale ko \(\underline{k}\) wale se multiply karein, aur teeno ko jama kar dein. Bas. Definition 1 ko angle chahiye, jo aksar maloom nahin hota; Definition 2 ko sirf components chahiye, jo sawal mein diye hote hain.
Lekin sawal yeh hai ke yeh dono definitions ek hi jawab kyun dein? Kitab yeh baat Example 5 mein plane ke liye saabit karti hai, aur 14.2.5 mein space ke liye Definition 2 ko derive karti hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\) aur \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - \underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\) ka dot product nikaalein.
Matching components multiply kar ke jama karein:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = (2)(1) + (3)(-1) + (-1)(4)\]
\[= 2 - 3 - 4 = -5\]
Jawab negative hai, is liye \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ke darmiyan angle obtuse (\(90^{\circ}\) se bara) hai. Dekha? Angle nikale baghair hi humein angle ki qisam pata chal gayi.
Ab kitab ka Example 5 dekhte hain, jo saabit karta hai ke dono definitions hamesha ek hi number deti hain.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem:
Prove that equivalence of following two definitions of dot product of two vectors:
(i) If \(\underline{v} = [x_{1}, y_{1}]\) and \(\underline{w} = [x_{2}, y_{2}]\) are two vectors in the plane, then \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{w} = x_{1}x_{2} + y_{1}y_{2}\)
(ii) If \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) are two non-zero vectors in the plane, then \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{w} = |\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) and \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{v} = [x_{1}, y_{1}]\), \(\underline{w} = [x_{2}, y_{2}]\), dono non-zero, aur in ke darmiyan angle \(\theta\).
To prove: \(x_{1}x_{2} + y_{1}y_{2} = |\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta\), yani dono definitions ek hi number deti hain.
Method: sab se pehle sochte hain ke \(\cos\theta\) aur lambaiyan (lengths) ek saath kis formula mein aati hain? Trigonometry ka law of cosines (cosine ka qanoon). Is liye \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) ko ek triangle ki do sides banayenge, teesri side par law of cosines lagayenge, aur phir lambaiyon ko components mein likhenge. Components likhte hi \(x_{1}x_{2} + y_{1}y_{2}\) khud ba khud saamne aa jayega.

Step 1: Triangle banayein
\(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) ko ek hi point se banayein. Teesri side \(\underline{w}\) ke sire (tip) ko \(\underline{v}\) ke sire se jorti hai; yeh vector \(\underline{v} - \underline{w}\) hai aur angle \(\theta\) ke bilkul saamne hai.
Kyun: head-to-tail rule se \(\underline{w} + (\underline{v} - \underline{w}) = \underline{v}\). Yani pehle \(\underline{w}\) par chalein, phir \(\underline{v} - \underline{w}\) par, to \(\underline{v}\) ke sire par pahunch jate hain. Is liye teesri side ki lambai \(|\underline{v} - \underline{w}|\) hai.
Dhyan dein: kitab ki figure mein is side ka teer (arrow) ulta laga hai; neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye. Proof sirf lambai istemal karta hai, is liye nateeja nahin badalta.

Step 2: Law of cosines lagayein
\[|\underline{v} - \underline{w}|^{2} = |\underline{v}|^{2} + |\underline{w}|^{2}\]
\[- 2|\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: kisi bhi triangle mein angle ke saamne wali side ka square = baqi do sides ke squares ka jor, minus 2 guna un do sides ka product guna cos(angle). Yeh Pythagoras ka bara bhai hai: \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\) ho to \(\cos\theta = 0\) aur yeh seedha Pythagoras ban jata hai.

Step 3: Har lambai ko components mein likhein
\[\underline{v} - \underline{w} = [x_{1} - x_{2},\ y_{1} - y_{2}]\]
\[|\underline{v} - \underline{w}|^{2} = (x_{1} - x_{2})^{2} + (y_{1} - y_{2})^{2}\]
\[|\underline{v}|^{2} = x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2},\quad |\underline{w}|^{2} = x_{2}^{2} + y_{2}^{2}\]
Kyun: vectors ko component by component (khana ba khana) tafreeq karte hain, aur magnitude ka square components ke squares ka jor hota hai. Ghor karein: magnitude ka square lene se square root khatam ho jata hai, is liye hisaab saaf rehta hai.

Step 4: (1) mein values rakhein
\[(x_{1} - x_{2})^{2} + (y_{1} - y_{2})^{2}\]
\[= (x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2}) + (x_{2}^{2} + y_{2}^{2})\]
\[- 2|\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta\]
Kyun: ab geometry wali equation (1) components ki equation ban gayi; ab sirf algebra baqi hai.

Step 5: Khol kar cancel karein
Left side kholne se:
\[x_{1}^{2} - 2x_{1}x_{2} + x_{2}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} - 2y_{1}y_{2} + y_{2}^{2}\]
Squares \(x_{1}^{2}, x_{2}^{2}, y_{1}^{2}, y_{2}^{2}\) dono taraf hain, is liye cancel ho jate hain:
\[-2x_{1}x_{2} - 2y_{1}y_{2} = -2|\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta\]
Kyun: \((a - b)^{2} = a^{2} - 2ab + b^{2}\). Equation ke dono taraf ek jaisi cheez ho to use dono taraf se hata sakte hain, jaise taraazu ke dono palron se barabar wazan utha lein to taraazu barabar hi rehta hai.

Step 6: \(-2\) se divide karein
\[x_{1}x_{2} + y_{1}y_{2} = |\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta\]
\[= \underline{v} \cdot \underline{w}\]
Kyun: dono taraf ko ek hi non-zero number se divide karne se equation sahi rehti hai. Ab left side definition (i) hai aur right side definition (ii). Dono barabar nikle, yahi saabit karna tha.

Tasdeeq:
Ek aasan misaal se dekhte hain: \(\underline{v} = [1, 0]\) aur \(\underline{w} = [1, 1]\). In ke darmiyan angle \(45^{\circ}\) hai (\(\underline{w}\) bilkul diagonal hai).
\[x_{1}x_{2} + y_{1}y_{2} = 1 + 0 = 1\]
\[|\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos 45^{\circ} = 1 \cdot \sqrt{2} \cdot \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1\]
Dono definitions \(1\) deti hain. Proof ke mutabiq bilkul aisa hi hona chahiye tha.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: dono definitions barabar hain, \(x_{1}x_{2} + y_{1}y_{2} = |\underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta = \underline{v} \cdot \underline{w}\).

blocks.alt: A triangle. Vector v runs along the base from the common starting point, vector w goes up from the same point making angle theta with v, and the third side, labelled v minus w, runs from the tip of w to the tip of v.
blocks.caption: Figure: the triangle formed by v, w and v − w (Example 5) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Example 5 wali figure mein \(\underline{v} - \underline{w}\) wali side par teer \(\underline{v}\) ke sire se \(\underline{w}\) ke sire ki taraf laga hai; yeh simt to \(\underline{w} - \underline{v}\) ki hai. Kyun ke \(\underline{w} + (\underline{v} - \underline{w}) = \underline{v}\), is liye \(\underline{v} - \underline{w}\) hamesha \(\underline{w}\) ke sire se \(\underline{v}\) ke sire ki taraf jata hai, jaisa hamari figure mein hai. Proof sirf lambai \(|\underline{v} - \underline{w}|\) istemal karta hai, jo dono soorton mein ek hi hai, is liye nateeja sahi rehta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\); vectors tail to tail, aur \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\).
2. Components se: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\).
3. Jawab scalar hai; doosre naam scalar product aur inner product.
4. Sign: acute angle par positive, right angle par zero, obtuse angle par negative.
5. Dono definitions barabar hain; is ka saboot law of cosines se aata hai (Example 5).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Components multiply kar ke jama karna bhool jana, aur jawab \(2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) jaisa likh dena. Dot product ek akela number hai.
2. Minus sign gum kar dena: \((3)(-1) = -3\). Bachne ka tareeqa: har product ko brackets mein likhein, phir hal karein.
3. Vectors head to tail rakh kar angle naapna; is se \(\pi - \theta\) mil jata hai aur sign ulat jata hai.
4. Yeh samajhna ke \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) mein \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ki lambaiyan nahin aatin. Aati hain: Definition 1 mein \(|\underline{u}|\) aur \(|\underline{v}|\) seedhe mojood hain.
